entries.test: Service-level subscription revenue, compute costs, and profitability would test whether every AI service loses money because it subsidizes compute.
entries.note: The statement explicitly attributes losses to compute subsidies.

entries.test: Anthropic's historical subscription allowances and compute costs, alongside AI startups' financial reports, would test the claimed subsidy and cash burn.
entries.note: Compute cost should not automatically be equated with retail API prices.

entries.test: Comparable task-level inference costs and token consumption across successive models would test whether reasoning-related token increases raised inference costs.
entries.note: The plain reading concerns total inference expense, not merely the price per token.

entries.test: Public evidence of a sustainably profitable monthly LLM subscription would contradict the universal economic infeasibility claim.
entries.note: The surrounding discussion gives 'does not make sense' a financial meaning.

entries.test: Historical subscription revenue and service costs for Copilot and other LLM services would test whether their monthly offerings were financially unsustainable.
entries.note: The proposition extracts the financial assertion from the accusation of swindling.

entries.test: A demonstrably sustainable LLM service that does not bill each user's actual token consumption would falsify the prediction.
entries.note: The proposition isolates the future portion of the assertion.

entries.test: Repeated public evaluations of LLM task execution and factual accuracy would test the claimed inability to guarantee reliable outcomes.
entries.note: The following paragraph clarifies unpredictability as unreliable task performance and factuality.
This is a hedged counterfactual about what past users would have done under different pricing.

entries.test: Published billing terms showing whether a majority of AI subscription offerings transition to token-based billing would test the prediction.
entries.note: 'I think' does not weaken the explicit assertion of inevitability.

entries.test: If Microsoft becomes financially unable to subsidize compute, public financial evidence that another company can sustain those subsidies would contradict the claim.
entries.note: Choosing to end subsidies would not itself establish inability to afford them.
'Closing time' specifies neither an outcome nor whose business ends. The proposition supplies 'the AI boom' as an interpretation.
'I'm not sure any' expresses doubt; it does not explicitly assert that absence of ROI is probable.
The dollar estimate is explicitly qualified by 'likely'.

entries.test: Public Claude Code usage logs and applicable token prices would show whether users of recent Anthropic models can spend $30 or less per active day.
entries.note: The categorical wording makes this testable despite its sweeping scope.

entries.test: Public budget decisions and management accounts would show whether cost-conscious businesses struggle to justify five- or six-figure AI expenses without demonstrated productivity gains.
entries.note: 'Nobody can seem to measure' does not establish that gains are inherently unmeasurable.

entries.test: Earnings calls, investor letters, and shareholder questions would show whether investors challenge rising AI-related R&D spending when revenue growth fails to follow.
entries.note: No deadline is given for the predicted investor reaction.
'This' refers to investor scrutiny when revenue growth fails to follow costs. The proposition drops that context, and the prediction is explicitly 'likely'.

entries.test: Public investor statements and funding reports around October 28, 2026 would show whether startups spending at least 10% of payroll on AI tokens face resistance over that spending.
entries.note: 'In six months' identifies a future point; 'within six months' changes it into a deadline window.
He expresses uncertainty about future hype, not a firm prediction of decline.
The post-contract earnings prediction is explicitly 'unlikely'. The years-to-pay-off assertion could be checked separately.

entries.test: Construction inventories, capacity commitments, and tenant contracts would establish OpenAI and Anthropic's share and the projects' financial exposure to them.
entries.note: In context, the percentage refers to demand for construction capacity.

entries.test: Recalculating the published model's revenues, expenses, depreciation, and debt payments would test its stated margins.
entries.note: This is a checkable model calculation, not an observed facility result. Whether principal repayments belong in gross margin is also checkable.

entries.test: Dated operational records and disclosed construction and equipment budgets would test Abilene's building status and estimated total cost.
entries.note: The proposition presents his personal cost estimate as an established approximate cost.

entries.test: Oracle's disclosed Stargate investment, operating results, and customer payments over the next several years would establish its time to profitability.
entries.note: 'Even if' makes timely payment a best-case concession, not a necessary antecedent.

entries.test: Abilene's announced delivery milestones and actual energized capacity as of April 2026 would establish whether the campus was behind schedule.
entries.note: This is an assertion about progress at publication.

entries.test: OpenAI's disclosed compute obligations, cumulative funding and revenue, and business growth through 2030 would test the asserted requirements for paying its contracts.
entries.note: The proposition omits the asserted annual growth requirement and the requirement to become cash-flow positive.

entries.test: OpenAI's financial results and scheduled Oracle payments would establish its losses and the gap between current revenue and ongoing obligations.
entries.note: The financial assertions have a plain reading despite the emphatic wording.

entries.test: If OpenAI cannot pay its Stargate bills, Oracle's subsequent solvency, bankruptcy filings, or business cessation would test the collapse prediction.
entries.note: 'Dies' has a plain financial-collapse reading in this context.

entries.test: Oracle's available capital, remaining project budgets, and partner commitments would establish the claimed funding shortfall.
entries.note: The quoted sentence names Stargate Abilene; the proposition substitutes Stargate generally. The surrounding discussion does not remove that scope mismatch.

entries.test: Stargate financing agreements, repayment terms, and tenant contracts would establish dependence on OpenAI and projected project cash flows.
entries.note: The proposition weakens 'entirely financed and paid for' to merely 'financed on' projected cash flow.

entries.test: If Anthropic runs out of money, disclosed losses and Google and Amazon's financial condition would show whether they absorb the loss without financial collapse.
entries.note: 'Can take the hit' asserts financial capacity, rather than a probability expressed by 'could'.

entries.test: Anthropic's compute agreements by the end of 2030 would establish whether meeting its commitments requires agreeing to annual spending of $25–100 billion.
entries.note: The source says 'agree to spend'; the proposition changes that to actual spending.

entries.test: Applying the stated PUE and revenue-per-megawatt assumptions to 15.2GW would test the annual revenue calculation and its financial rationale.
entries.note: The proposition omits the explicit modeling assumptions. The 2028 date describes expected construction completion, not a forecast deadline for this calculation.

entries.test: Public financial results, unit economics, and funded business plans would test whether either company has a financially viable route to profitability.
entries.note: This is a categorical financial assertion about their current businesses.

entries.test: Compute providers' customer revenues and those customers' operating cash flows and financing sources would establish dependence on continued venture funding and debt.
entries.note: Dependence of a large share is asserted firmly; only the additional majority claim is hedged.

entries.test: Cursor's January 2026 revenue and cost-of-service figures, including and excluding free users, would establish the two gross margins.
entries.note: The financial figures are asserted in Zitron's own voice.

entries.test: AI data-center financial results at less than full utilization and tenancy would show whether they lose millions and make no progress recovering capital costs.
entries.note: 'Fail to chip away' asserts no progress; 'fail to cover depreciation' can mean only incomplete coverage.
'Tantamount to fraud' is an evaluative characterization here, without a specified false representation or legal test.
The source asserts a present private intention. The proposition changes that into a firm prediction of future action.

entries.test: Public release statements, capacity records, and technical evaluations would test whether capacity constraints rather than exceptional capabilities explain Mythos's restricted release.
entries.note: 'Nothingburger' expresses dismissal, not a defined technical claim that the model is ordinary. The asserted operational explanation remains testable.

entries.test: Published commercial terms for code-generating LLM products would show whether their subscription offerings disappear entirely.
entries.note: This is a firm prediction with no deadline.

entries.test: OpenAI's historical growth rates and contractual obligations would test the claimed slowdown and required tenfold business expansion by 2030.
entries.note: Something occurring before a company starts dying is not the same as evidence that the company is already dying.
Whether AI's outcomes justify its existence is a judgment of worth, even though reliability and financial performance can be tested separately.
The industry's 'fall' has no shared threshold distinguishing contraction, lost enthusiasm, bankruptcies, or disappearance.
He asks readers to consider this scenario rather than asserting that it will happen.

entries.test: OpenAI's cumulative revenue and funding through 2030, Stargate payments, Oracle's stock performance, and disclosed Ellison margin calls would test the predicted chain.
entries.note: The antecedent has an explicit end-of-2030 deadline; the resulting financial consequences have no separate deadline.
